subject: Request: Exceptional renewal discount for CuraTech - VP/CFO signoff
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Julie Park <julie@curatech.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Exceptional renewal discount for CuraTech - VP/CFO signoff

Team —

Quick background: CuraTech is at the end of year-2 on a pilot-to-enterprise path. They signed initially for $150k ARR, moved to a $750k annualized pilot last year, and now are preparing to convert to a committed $1.2M ARR renewal (12‑month). They are asking for a one-time accelerated renewal discount to secure committed spend and expand into two additional product modules in Q2.

Commercial ask: 45% headline discount off list for year 1 with a fixed minimum monthly invoice (to protect unit economics). They want signature this week to align with their board renewal meeting.

Why I’m escalating: 45% exceeds standard delegated authority and our normal high-touch concession guardrails. I’ve attached the SOW and a simple pricing model showing the blended unit cost at the requested discount. Key points:
- Committed ARR: $1,200,000 (12 months)
- Requested discount: 45% (one-year term)
- Upside: commit to 2 extra modules + a 12‑month auto-renew clause; target net retention >130% in year 2
- Risk: unit economics under 30% gross margin in our baseline serving assumptions; contract would need explicit usage guards (seat caps and overage rates)

Options I propose for signoff (ranked by preference):
1) Approve 45% limited to year-1 only, require seat/usage hard caps and standard overage pricing thereafter; immediate DocuSign.
2) Approve a lower exceptional discount (30%) with a $150k onboarding credit and a 24‑month staged renewal (year 2 at list minus 10%).
3) Decline and propose a counter at 25% with strong expansion milestones tied to credits.

Request: need VP/CFO signoff to proceed on option 1 or 2. If you authorize, I’ll draft the final SOW and send to CuraTech legal for a fast-track DocuSign.

Attachments: CuraTech_SOW_v2.pdf, curatech-pricing-model.xlsx

Thanks,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Julie Park <julie@curatech.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Feb 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Exceptional renewal discount for CuraTech - VP/CFO signoff

Rafael —

Thanks for the context and the attachments. A few quick clarifying questions before I involve CFO:
1) Is the 45% request purely on list price across all SKUs or targeted to the base inference service?
2) What are the required usage caps / contractual guardrails you think are non‑negotiable? Please add concrete thresholds.
3) Do we have reference metrics on how likely CuraTech is to hit the expansion milestones in 6 months? Any letter of intent?

I’m copying Marissa (Finance lead for Commercial exceptions) so she can weigh in on tolerance for a one-time deep concession vs a staged structure. If Marissa and Priyom are comfortable, I’ll escalate to CFO for signoff.

If this is time-sensitive, Rafael, can you confirm whether CuraTech will walk if we counter with option 2 (30% + onboarding credit)?

-Kimberly
VP, Sales Operations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Julie Park <julie@curatech.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Feb 2028 13:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Exceptional renewal discount for CuraTech - VP/CFO signoff

Kimberly / Rafael —

Reviewed the SOW and the pricing model. I appreciate the upfront mitigation language in the spreadsheet. My read: CuraTech is strategic and the expansion upside is credible, but 45% is beyond our long-term margin comfort without stronger safeguards. I can support a conditional exception with the following binding terms: 

- Approve a 35% one‑time headline discount (finalized in DocuSign) for year 1 only.
- Include hard usage caps (monthly token cap tied to a defined seat count) and explicit 150% overage multiplier for any consumption above the cap.
- Provide a $100,000 onboarding credit (applied against month 1–3 invoices) that is non-refundable and clawed back if expansion milestones are not met by month 9.
- Add a 12‑month auto-renew at a minimum of list minus 10% (unless renegotiated with renewed CFO approval).

Rationale: 35% plus operational protections preserves a path to acceptable unit economics, gives the customer value to sign now, and keeps us protected on tail risk. This requires CFO signoff to be binding; I recommend we present this as our final commercial concession.

Next steps: If Priyom (legal) is ok with the clawback language, Kimberly — please escalate to CFO (copying finance distribution) with the attached SOW and the one‑page commercial memo I’ve created (I’ll upload to HubSpot). Rafael — please confirm CuraTech will accept a 35% headline if we include the terms above (we need a verbal now, written in DocuSign by EOD).

Marissa Cole
Head of Finance, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Julie Park <julie@curatech.com>, CuraTech Legal <legal@curatech.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Feb 2028 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Exceptional renewal discount for CuraTech - VP/CFO signoff

Thanks — I just spoke with Julie (CuraTech CEO) and they indicated the board will approve at 35% + $100k onboarding credit if we lock the SOW this week and include the seat caps / clawback. They understand the auto-renew at list minus 10% for year 2.

I’ll update the SOW with the exact cap numbers (proposed monthly token cap = 75M tokens; seat definition attached) and route the final DocuSign to legal. If Marissa and Kimberly approve, please confirm authorization string for CFO signoff so I can close the loop.

If we get the green light, next actions:
- Marissa: final memo uploaded to HubSpot for CFO packet (I’ll add link).
- Priyom: please comment on the clawback wording; we need an enforceable repayment mechanism.
- Kimberly: I’ll coordinate DocuSign and ask CuraTech legal to countersign.

Standing by for the CFO authorization phrase — Rafael Mendes authorized to bind commercial terms per Marissa Cole direction (example string).

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
